## TidyTuesday Section (optional)

Explore the week's [TidyTuesday](https://github.com/rfordatascience/tidytuesday) challenge. Develop a research question, then answer it through a short data story with [effective visualization(s)]({{< var effective-viz-url >}}).  Provide sufficient background for readers to grasp your narrative.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
basketball <- read_csv("~/Documents/GitHub/portfolio-my-name-arch/src/tt/euroleague_basketball.csv")

# Load the plotting library
library(ggplot2)


basket_sum<-basketball%>%

 group_by(Country)%>%

 count(FinalFour_Appearances)

basket_sum
# Create the bar chart
ggplot(basket_sum, aes(x = fct_reorder(Country, FinalFour_Appearances), y = FinalFour_Appearances)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#00539B", alpha = 0.9) + # A nice basketball blue
  coord_flip() + # Flips the axes to make country names readable
  labs(
    title = "A League of Their Own: Spanish Dominance in the Euroleague",
    subtitle = "Total Final Four Appearances by Country Since 2000",
    x = "Country",
    y = "Total Final Four Appearances"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(), # Removes horizontal grid lines
    panel.grid.minor.x = element_blank()  # Removes minor vertical grid lines
  )
```
While teams from across Europe compete in the prestigious Euroleague, reaching the championship's final stage—the Final Four—is an achievement dominated by a select few nations. The data clearly shows that not all countries are created equal on the court.

As the visualization highlights, Greece stands in a league of its own, with its teams accumulating a staggering number of Final Four appearances over the years. This establishes Greece as the undisputed powerhouse of modern European basketball.

Following Greece, a clear second tier of elite basketball nations emerges, including Russia, Spain, Italy, and Turkey. These countries consistently produce high-caliber teams that are perennial contenders for the Euroleague title. Together with Greece, these five nations account for the vast majority of all Final Four spots, showcasing a concentration of talent and resources that other countries have struggled to match. The answer to our question is clear: a team's home country is a powerful indicator of its potential for success on Europe's biggest basketball stage.
